summary: The belt adds one inbox scan (sha256 per file, CRLF-normalized) to each git commit issued through a session; the never-scanned empty inbox short-circuits before any hashing or mkdir, so repos without a context inbox pay a stat-level cost only. Subprocess use is a single fixed-argv git add on the drift path.

non_blocking_findings.summary: scan_inbox rehashes every inbox file on each commit rather than short-circuiting on mtime/size; bounded by the 5MB per-file inbox cap and typical inbox sizes (~67 files at minegate, ~3s worst case observed in tests), so a cache is not warranted yet.
